title: Retirement
hook: a new season of service and prayer
tomorrow: why does a rumor need you to keep it alive?

segments.voice: Yesterday, stopping: rest set by the calendar, given to the whole household, even the donkey, finished or not. The line was stop on time.

A sheet cake in the break room. A card signed by everyone, most of it saying relax, you've earned it. A last walk out to the car. And then a quiet Monday, with nowhere to be by eight, and a question that can sneak up on anyone who worked a long time: so what am I for now? The card doesn't answer it. The question is old. So is the answer.
screen: `A CAKE AND A CARD.` → `A QUIET MONDAY.` → `WHAT AM I FOR NOW?`

segments.voice: One answer comes in an old person's own voice, in the Psalms. In the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Cast me not off in the time of old age: when my strength shall fail, do not thou forsake me." Then the same psalm asks for time for one more job: to show God's strength to the generation that is to come. Old age with an assignment. Luke shows it in Anna, a widow who never left the Temple, serving with fasting and prayer night and day, who saw the child Jesus and spoke of him to everyone who was waiting. Saint John Paul the Second wrote a letter to elderly people when he was old himself, and called them keepers of a living memory, with something to pass on. Prayer, service, handing things down: a new season, not a closed door. A neighbor tradition gives this season a name. In Hindu tradition, the Laws of Manu describe the stages of a life: when a householder sees his skin wrinkled, his hair white, and his children's children, he may turn toward the forest. That stage is called vanaprastha, a life given more to prayer and less to getting. Here Catholics and Hindus share a picture: the later years as a turn toward the spirit, not a slide into nothing. The difference is honest. The classic Hindu stage steps back from household and town; the psalmist asks to stay right among the young, telling them.
screen: `CAST ME NOT OFF IN OLD AGE.` · `ANNA: NIGHT AND DAY.` · `A LIVING MEMORY TO PASS ON.` · `VANAPRASTHA: TOWARD THE FOREST.` · then, large: `A NEW SEASON.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who has retired: a grandparent, a teacher, a coach, a neighbor. Send them one line naming something they handed down to you, a skill, a saying, a way of doing things. Name it as specifically as you can: not thanks for everything, but the one thing. If you pray, you can hold them before God for a moment after it sends.
Retirement. The end of a working life, and in Catholic eyes the start of a season of prayer, service and handing on.
Hold on to this: a new season, like the psalmist asking for time to tell the young. Go gently.

howItsDone: In parishes, retired members often serve as lectors, visitors to the sick, catechists and people who pray for the parish; the Church celebrates a World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly in July.

chat.meaning: The psalmist asks for time to show God's strength to the generation to come, and Anna served night and day. Retirement can open a season of prayer and handing on.

notes: Douay-Rheims Psalm 70:9 quoted from memory; confirm exact Challoner wording. Psalm 70:18 paraphrased ('unto old age and grey hairs... until I shew forth thy arm to all the generation that is to come').

Luke 2:36–38 (Anna) paraphrased: departed not from the temple, by fastings and prayers serving night and day; spoke of him to all that looked for the redemption of Israel. Her age is not stated in the voice. Confirm.
John Paul II, Letter to the Elderly (1999), paraphrased: written 'as an elderly person myself'; the elderly as guardians of collective memory, with wisdom to pass on. Confirm wording and section.

v3 unity thread (wisdom day): Laws of Manu 6.2 paraphrased (when a householder sees his skin wrinkled, his hair white, and the sons of his sons, he may resort to the forest; Bühler 1886 is the public-domain English, not quoted). Shared ground: the later years as a turn toward the spirit. Honest difference: the classic vanaprastha steps back from household and town; Psalm 71 asks to stay among the young, telling them. Please have a Hindu reader confirm the framing is fair, and note that some Hindus contest the authority of the Manusmriti; the term vanaprastha also appears in other texts if a different source is preferred.

howItsDone: the World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly (instituted by Pope Francis, celebrated near the feast of Sts. Joachim and Anne in July). Confirm; 'many parishes rely on retired members' is a general description, not a statistic: soften if needed.
